page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n2 server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the x86_64 architecture and includes L1d, L2, and L3 caches of 32 KB, 1.0 MB, and 33 MB respectively. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the lower performance tiers for most compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1398.19, and the multi-core score is 1837.38, both reflecting lower-tier processing capacity. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 13.8 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.79 GB/sec. However, single-threaded gzip compression shows average performance at 23.81 GB/sec. Geekbench scores further confirm these characteristics, with a single-core score of 1123.0 and a multi-core score of 1333.0.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but modest overall compute and memory bandwidth, the n2-standard-2 is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads. These include basic web serving, small-scale text processing, and minor database operations. It is not designed for intensive tasks like large-scale LLM inference, compiling complex software, or ray tracing, where benchmarks indicate poor performance. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, it offers an entry-level dedicated resource profile for workloads that require predictable CPU allocation without the overhead of high-performance hardware.
